terms.gloss: an algorithm; at first, reckoning with Arabic numerals
evidence: M-O s.v. algorithm: algorismus, i m. (1698 Hofmann s.v. algebra)
terms.comment: The medieval word, from the name of the Persian mathematician al-Khwārizmī; it first named the art of reckoning with Arabic numerals, and gave the modern word. Not in Lewis & Short. Its vowels are left unmarked: we have found no source for their quantity.
The plain classical word for a method or system (see approach, method); certa ratiō, a fixed method, says what an algorithm is.

phrases.latin: Algorismus est certa ratiō, quā rēs gradātim efficitur.
phrases.english: An algorithm is a fixed method by which something is done step by step.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. algorithm.
Lewis & Short: ratio
